entries.1e19f333d5e90e051cc4fa4cabd0e4539a623773: <div sID="gen20456" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="5" osisID="Mic.5" sID="Mic.5"/> <div eID="gen20456" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20457" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen20458" type="x-p"/> In this chapter we have, I. A prediction of the troubles and distresses of the Jewish nation, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.1">ver. 1</reference>. II. A promise of the Messiah, and of his kingdom, to support the people of God in the day of these troubles. 1. Of the birth of the Messiah, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.4">ver. 4</reference>. 3. Of his protection of his people, and his victory over his and their enemies, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.5-Mic.5.6">ver. 5, 6</reference>. 4. Of the great world by it, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.7">ver. 7</reference>. 5. Of the destruction of the enemies of the church, both those without, that attack it, and those within, that expose it, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.8-Mic.5.15">ver. 8-15</reference>.
entries.32bc728e6ed56ecb9eb63e4dfeae6cebe10a3f5e: <div eID="gen20458" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen20457" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Abasement and Distress of Zion; Birth of the Messiah Predicted; The Glory of Messiah. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi>  720.)</title> <div sID="gen20459" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> Now gather thyself in troops, O daughter of troops: he hath laid siege against us: they shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek. <hi type="super">2</hi> But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, <hi type="italic">though</hi> thou be little among the thousands of Judah, <hi type="italic">yet</hi> out of thee shall he come forth unto me <hi type="italic">that is</hi> to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth <hi type="italic">have been</hi> from of old, from everlasting. <hi type="super">3</hi> Therefore will he give them up, until the time <hi type="italic">that</hi> she which travaileth hath brought forth: then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel. <hi type="super">4</hi> And he shall stand and feed in the strength of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , in the majesty of the name of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> his God; and they shall abide: for now shall he be great unto the ends of the earth. <hi type="super">5</hi> And this <hi type="italic">man</hi> shall be the peace, when the Assyrian shall come into our land: and when he shall tread in our palaces, then shall we raise against him seven shepherds, and eight principal men. <hi type="super">6</hi> And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof: thus shall he deliver <hi type="italic">us</hi> from the Assyrian, when he cometh into our land, and when he treadeth within our borders. <div eID="gen20459" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20460" type="x-p"/> Here, as before, we have, <div eID="gen20460" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20461" type="x-p"/> I. The abasement and distress of Zion, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.1">v. 1</reference>. The Jewish nation, for many years before the captivity, dwindled, and fell into disgrace: <hi type="italic">Now gather thyself in troops, O daughter of troops!</hi> It is either a summons to Zion's enemies, that had troops at their service, to come and do their worst against her (God will suffer them to do it), or a challenge to Zion's friends, that had troops too at command, to come and do their best for her; Let them <hi type="italic">gather in troops,</hi> yet it shall be to no purpose; for, says the prophet, in the name of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, <hi type="italic">He has laid siege against us;</hi> the king of Assyria has, the king of Babylon has, and we know not which way to defend ourselves; so that the enemies shall gain their point, and prevail so far as <hi type="italic">to smite the judge of Israel</hi>—the king, the chief justice, and the other inferior judges—<hi type="italic">with a rod upon the cheek,</hi> in contempt of them and their dignity; having made them prisoners, they shall use them as shamefully as any of the common captives. Complaint had been made of the judges of Israel (<reference osisRef="Mic.3.11">ch. iii. 11</reference>) that they were corrupt and took bribes, and this disgrace came justly upon them for abusing their power; yet it was a great calamity to Israel to have their judges treated thus ignominiously. Some make this the reason why the troops (that is, the Roman army) shall lay siege to Jerusalem, because the Jews <hi type="italic">shall smite the judge of Israel upon the cheek,</hi> because of the indignities they shall do to the Messiah, the Judge of Israel, whom they smote on the cheek, saying, <hi type="italic">Prophesy, who smote thee.</hi> But the former sense seems more probable, and that it is meant of the besieging of Jerusalem, not by the Romans, but the Chaldeans, and was fulfilled in the indignities done to king Zedekiah and the princes of the house of David. <div eID="gen20461" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20462" type="x-p"/> II. The advancement of Zion's King. Having shown how low the house of David should be brought, and how vilely the shield of that mighty family should be cast away, as though it had not been anointed with oil, to encourage the faith of God's people, who might be tempted now to think that his covenant with David and his house was abrogated (according to the psalmist's complaint, <reference osisRef="Ps.89.38-Ps.89.39">Ps. lxxxix. 38, 39</reference>), he adds an illustrious prediction of the Messiah and his kingdom, in whom that covenant should be established, and the honours of that house should be revived, advanced, and perpetuated. Now let us see, <div eID="gen20462" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20463" type="x-p"/> 1. How the Messiah is here described. It is he that is to be <hi type="italic">ruler in Israel, whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting,</hi> from the <hi type="italic">days of eternity,</hi> as the word is. Here we have, (1.) His existence from eternity, as God: <hi type="italic">his goings forth,</hi> or <hi type="italic">emanations,</hi> as the going forth of the beams from the sun, were, or have been, <hi type="italic">of old, from everlasting,</hi> which (says Dr. Pocock) is so signal a description of Christ's eternal generation, or his going forth as the Son of God, begotten of his Father before all worlds, that this prophecy must belong only to him, and could never be verified of any other. It certainly speaks of a going forth that was now past, when the prophet spoke, and cannot but be read, as we read it, his <hi type="italic">outgoings have been;</hi> and the putting of both these words together, which severally are used to denote eternity, plainly shows that they must here be taken in the strictest sense (the same with <reference osisRef="Ps.90.2">Ps. xc. 2</reference>, <hi type="italic">From everlasting to everlasting thou are God</hi>), and can be applied to no other than to him who was able to say, <hi type="italic">Before Abraham was, I am,</hi> <reference osisRef="John.8.58">John viii. 58</reference>. Dr. Pocock observes that the <hi type="italic">going forth</hi> is used (<reference osisRef="Deut.8.3">Deut. viii. 3</reference>) for a <hi type="italic">word</hi> which <hi type="italic">proceeds out of the mouth,</hi> and is therefore very fitly used to signify the eternal generation of him who is called the <hi type="italic">Word of God,</hi> that was <hi type="italic">in the beginning with God,</hi> <reference osisRef="John.1.1-John.1.2">John i. 1, 2</reference>. (2.) His office as Mediator; he was to be <hi type="italic">ruler in Israel,</hi> king of his church; he was to <hi type="italic">reign over the house of Jacob for ever,</hi> <reference osisRef="Luke.1.32-Luke.1.33">Luke i. 32, 33</reference>. The Jews object that our Lord Jesus could not be the Messiah, for he was so far from being ruler in Israel that Israel ruled over him, and put him to death, and would not have him to reign over them; but he answered that himself when he said, <hi type="italic">My kingdom is not of this world,</hi> <reference osisRef="John.18.36">John xviii. 36</reference>. And it is a spiritual Israel that he reigns over, the children of promise, all the followers of believing Abraham and praying Jacob. In the hearts of these he reigns by his Spirit and grace, and in the society of these by his word and ordinances. And was not he <hi type="italic">ruler in Israel</hi> whom winds and seas obeyed, to whom legions of devils were forced to submit, and who commanded away diseases from the sick and called the dead out of their graves? None but he whose <hi type="italic">goings forth were from of old, from everlasting,</hi> was fit to be <hi type="italic">ruler in Israel,</hi> to be head of the church, and <hi type="italic">head over all things to the church.</hi> <div eID="gen20463" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20464" type="x-p"/> 2. What is here foretold concerning him. <div eID="gen20464" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20465" type="x-p"/> (1.) That Bethlehem should be the place of his nativity, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.2">v. 2</reference>. This was the scripture which the scribes went upon when with the greatest assurance they told Herod <hi type="italic">where Christ should be born</hi> (<reference osisRef="Matt.2.6">Matt. ii. 6</reference>), and hence it was universally known among the Jews that <hi type="italic">Christ should come out of the town of Bethlehem where David was,</hi> <reference osisRef="John.7.42">John vii. 42</reference>. <hi type="italic">Beth-lehem</hi> signifies <hi type="italic">the house of bread,</hi> the fittest place for him to be born in who is <hi type="italic">the bread of life.</hi> And, because it was the city of David, by a special providence it was ordered that he should be born there who was to be the <hi type="italic">Son of David,</hi> and his heir and successor for ever. It is called <hi type="italic">Bethlehem-Ephratah,</hi> both names of the same city, as appears <reference osisRef="Gen.35.19">Gen. xxxv. 19</reference>. It was <hi type="italic">little among the thousands of Judah,</hi> not considerable either for the number of the inhabitants or the figure they made; it had nothing in it worthy to have this honour put upon it; but God in that, as in other instances, chose to <hi type="italic">exalt those of low degree,</hi> <reference osisRef="Luke.1.52">Luke i. 52</reference>. Christ would give honour to the place of his birth, and not derive honour from it: <hi type="italic">Though thou be little,</hi> yet this shall make thee great, and, as St. Matthew reads it, Thou <hi type="italic">art not the least among the princes of Judah,</hi> but upon this account art really honourable above any of them. A relation to Christ will magnify those that are little in the world. <div eID="gen20465" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20466" type="x-p"/> (2.) That in the fulness of time he should be born of a woman (<reference osisRef="Mic.5.3">v. 3</reference>): <hi type="italic">Therefore will he give them up;</hi> he will give up his people Israel to distress and trouble, and will defer their salvation, which has been so long promised and expected, <hi type="italic">until the time,</hi> the set time, <hi type="italic">that she who travails has brought forth,</hi> or (as it should be read) <hi type="italic">that she who shall bring forth shall have brought forth,</hi> that the blessed virgin, who was to be the mother of the Messiah, shall have brought him forth at Bethlehem, the place appointed. This Dr. Pocock thinks to be the most genuine sense of the words. Though the out-goings of the Messiah were <hi type="italic">from everlasting,</hi> yet the <hi type="italic">redemption in Jerusalem,</hi> the <hi type="italic">consolation of Israel,</hi> must be <hi type="italic">waited for</hi> (<reference osisRef="Luke.2.25-Luke.2.38">Luke ii. 25-38</reference>) until the time that <hi type="italic">she who should bring forth</hi> (so the virgin Mary is called, as Christ is himself called, <hi type="italic">He that shall come</hi>) shall <hi type="italic">bring forth;</hi> and in the mean time <hi type="italic">he will give them up.</hi> Divine salvations must be waited for until the time fixed for the bringing of them forth. <div eID="gen20466" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20467" type="x-p"/> (3.) That <hi type="italic">the remnant of his brethren shall then return to the children of Israel.</hi> The remnant of the Jewish nation shall return to the spirit of the true genuine children of Israel, a people in covenant with God; the hearts of the children shall be turned to the fathers, <reference osisRef="Mal.4.6">Mal. iv. 6</reference>. Some understand it of all believers, Gentiles as well as Jews; they shall all be incorporated into the commonwealth of Israel; and, as they are all brethren to one another, so <hi type="italic">he is not ashamed to call them brethren,</hi> <reference osisRef="Heb.2.11">Heb. ii. 11</reference>. <div eID="gen20467" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20468" type="x-p"/> (4.) That he shall be a glorious prince, and his subjects shall be happy under his government (<reference osisRef="Mic.5.4">v. 4</reference>): <hi type="italic">He shall stand and feed,</hi> that is, he shall both teach and rule, and continue to do so, as a good shepherd, with wisdom, and care, and love. So it was foretold. <hi type="italic">He shall feed his flock like a shepherd,</hi> shall provide green pastures for them, and under-shepherds to lead them into these pastures. He is the <hi type="italic">good shepherd</hi> that <hi type="italic">goes before the sheep,</hi> and presides among them. He shall do this, not as an ordinary man, but <hi type="italic">in the strength of the Lord,</hi> as one clothed with a divine power to go through his work, and break through the difficulties in his way, so as not to <hi type="italic">fail,</hi> or be <hi type="italic">discouraged;</hi> he shall do it <hi type="italic">in the majesty of the name of the Lord his God,</hi> so as plainly to evidence that <hi type="italic">God's name was in him</hi> (<reference osisRef="Exod.23.21">Exod. xxiii. 21</reference>) the majesty of his name, for <hi type="italic">he taught as one having authority and not as the scribes.</hi> The prophets prefaced their messages with, <hi type="italic">Thus saith the Lord;</hi> but Christ spoke, not as a servant, but as a Son—<hi type="italic">Verily, verily, I say unto you.</hi> This was feeding <hi type="italic">in the majesty of the name of the Lord his God. All power was given him in heaven and in earth,</hi> a <hi type="italic">power over all flesh,</hi> by virtue of which he still rules <hi type="italic">in the majesty of the name of the Lord his God,</hi> a name above every name. Christ's government shall be, [1.] Very happy for his subjects, for <hi type="italic">they shall abide;</hi> they shall be safe and easy, and continue so for ever. <hi type="italic">Because he lives, they shall live also.</hi> They shall lie down in the green pastures to which he shall lead them, <hi type="italic">shall abide in God's tabernacle for ever,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ps.61.4">Ps. lxi. 4</reference>. His church shall abide, and he in it, and with it, always, even to the end of the world. [2.] It shall be very glorious to himself: <hi type="italic">Now shall he be great to the ends of the earth.</hi> Now that he stands and feeds his flock, <hi type="italic">now shall he be great.</hi> For Christ reckons it his greatness to do good. Now he shall be <hi type="italic">great to the ends of the earth,</hi> for the uttermost parts of the earth shall be given him for his possession, and the ends of the world shall see his salvation. <div eID="gen20468" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20469" type="x-p"/> (5) That he shall secure the peace and welfare of his church and people against all the attempts of his and their enemies (<reference osisRef="Mic.5.5-Mic.5.6">v. 5, 6</reference>): <hi type="italic">This man,</hi> as king and ruler, <hi type="italic">shall be the peace when the Assyrians shall come into our land.</hi> This refers to the deliverance of Hezekiah and his kingdom from the power of Sennacherib, who invaded them, in the type; but, under the shadow of that, it is a promise of the safety of the gospel-church and of all believers from the designs and attempts of the powers of darkness, Satan and all his instruments, the dragon and his angels, that seek to devour the church of the first-born and all that belong to it. Observe, [1.] The peril and danger which Christ's subjects are supposed to be in. The Assyrian, a potent enemy, <hi type="italic">comes into their land</hi> (<reference osisRef="Mic.5.5-Mic.5.6">v. 5, 6</reference>), <hi type="italic">treads within their borders,</hi> nay, prevails so far as to <hi type="italic">tread in their palaces;</hi> it was a time of <hi type="italic">treading down and of perplexity</hi> when Sennacherib made a descent upon Judah, took all the defenced cities, and laid siege to Jerusalem, <reference osisRef="Isa.36.1">Isa. xxxvi. 1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.37.3">xxxvii. 3</reference>. This represented the gates of hell fighting against the kingdom of Christ, <hi type="italic">encompassing the camp of the saints and of the holy city,</hi> and threatening to bear down all before them. When the terrors of the law set themselves in array against a convinced soul, when the temptations of Satan assault the people of God, and the troubles of the world threaten to rob them of all their comforts, then the <hi type="italic">Assyrian comes into their land</hi> and treads in their palaces. <hi type="italic">Without are fightings, within are fears.</hi> [2.] The protection and defence which his subjects are then sure to be under. <hi type="italic">First,</hi> Christ will himself be <hi type="italic">their peace.</hi> When the Assyrian comes with such a force into a land, can there be any other peace than a tame submission and an unresisted desolation? Yes, even then the church's King will be the conservator of the church's peace, will be <hi type="italic">for a hiding-place,</hi> <reference osisRef="Isa.32.1-Isa.32.2">Isa. xxxii. 1, 2</reference>. Christ is our peace as a priest, making atonement for sin, and reconciling us to God; and he is our peace as a king, conquering our enemies and commanding down disquieting fears and passions; he <hi type="italic">creates the fruit of the lips, peace.</hi> Even when the Assyrian comes into the land, when we are in the greatest distress and danger and have received a sentence of death within ourselves, yet <hi type="italic">this man may be the peace. In me,</hi> says Christ, <hi type="italic">you shall have peace,</hi> when <hi type="italic">in the world you have tribulation;</hi> at such a time our souls may dwell at ease in him. <hi type="italic">Secondly,</hi> He will find out proper instruments to be employed for their protection and deliverance, and the defeat of their enemies: <hi type="italic">Then shall we raise against him seven shepherds and eight principal men,</hi> that is, a competent number of persons, proper to oppose the enemy, and make head against him, and protect the church of God in peace, men that shall have the care and tenderness of shepherds and the courage and authority of <hi type="italic">principal men,</hi> or <hi type="italic">princes of men. Seven</hi> and <hi type="italic">eight</hi> are a certain number for an uncertain. Note, When God has work to do he will not want fitting instruments to do it with; and when he pleases he can do it by a few; he needs not raise thousands, but seven or eight principal men may serve the turn if God be with them. Magistrates and ministers are shepherds and principal men, raised in defence of religion's righteous cause against the powers of sin and Satan in the world. <hi type="italic">Thirdly,</hi> The opposition given to the church shall be got over, and the opposers brought down. This is represented by the laying of Assyria and Chaldea waste, which two nations were the most formidable enemies to the Israel of God of any, and the destruction of them signified the making of Christ's enemies his footstool: <hi type="italic">They shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof;</hi> they shall make inroads upon the land, and put to the sword all that they find in arms. Note, Those that threaten ruin to the church of God hasten ruin to themselves; and their destruction is the church's salvation: <hi type="italic">Thus</hi> shall he <hi type="italic">deliver us from the Assyrian.</hi> When <hi type="italic">Satan fell as lightning from heaven</hi> before the preaching of the gospel, and Christ's enemies, that would not have him to reign over them, were <hi type="italic">slain before him,</hi> then this was fulfilled.
entries.13166b2bc31d0c71e676fc82047cd85c212d3657: <div eID="gen20469" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Increase of the Church; Encouraging Predictions. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 720.)</title> <div sID="gen20470" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">7</hi> And the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many people as a dew from the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , as the showers upon the grass, that tarrieth not for man, nor waiteth for the sons of men. <hi type="super">8</hi> And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many people as a lion among the beasts of the forest, as a young lion among the flocks of sheep: who, if he go through, both treadeth down, and teareth in pieces, and none can deliver. <hi type="super">9</hi> Thine hand shall be lifted up upon thine adversaries, and all thine enemies shall be cut off. <hi type="super">10</hi> And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , that I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee, and I will destroy thy chariots: <hi type="super">11</hi> And I will cut off the cities of thy land, and throw down all thy strong holds: <hi type="super">12</hi> And I will cut off witchcrafts out of thine hand; and thou shalt have no <hi type="italic">more</hi> soothsayers: <hi type="super">13</hi> Thy graven images also will I cut off, and thy standing images out of the midst of thee; and thou shalt no more worship the work of thine hands. <hi type="super">14</hi> And I will pluck up thy groves out of the midst of thee: so will I destroy thy cities. <hi type="super">15</hi> And I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen, such as they have not heard. <div eID="gen20470" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20471" type="x-p"/> Glorious things are here spoken of <hi type="italic">the remnant of Jacob,</hi> that remnant which was raised of <hi type="italic">her that halted</hi> (<reference osisRef="Mic.4.7">ch. iv. 7</reference>), and it seems to be that <hi type="italic">remnant which the Lord our God shall call</hi> (<reference osisRef="Joel.2.32">Joel ii. 32</reference>), on whom the Spirit shall be poured out, the remnant that shall be saved, <reference osisRef="Rom.9.27">Rom. ix. 27</reference>. Note, God's people are but a remnant, a small number in comparison with the many that are left to perish, a <hi type="italic">little flock;</hi> but they are <hi type="italic">the remnant of Jacob,</hi> a people in covenant with God, and in his favour. Now concerning this remnant it is here promised, <div eID="gen20471" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20472" type="x-p"/> I. That they shall be <hi type="italic">as a dew</hi> in the midst of the nations, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.7">v. 7</reference>. God's church is dispersed all the world over; it is <hi type="italic">in the midst of many people,</hi> as gold in the ore, wheat in the heap. Israel according to the flesh dwelt alone, and was not numbered among the nations; but the spiritual Israel lies scattered <hi type="italic">in the midst of many people,</hi> as the <hi type="italic">salt of the earth,</hi> or as seed sown in the ground, here a grain and there a grain, <reference osisRef="Hos.2.23">Hos. ii. 23</reference>. Now this remnant shall be <hi type="italic">as dew from the Lord.</hi> 1. They shall be of a heavenly extraction; as <hi type="italic">dew from the Lord,</hi> who is the <hi type="italic">Father of the rain,</hi> and has <hi type="italic">begotten the drops of the dew,</hi> <reference osisRef="Job.38.28">Job xxxviii. 28</reference>. They are <hi type="italic">born from above,</hi> and are not of the earth, savouring the things of the earth. 2. They shall be numerous as the drops of dew in a summer's morning. <reference osisRef="Ps.110.3">Ps. cx. 3</reference>, <hi type="italic">Thou hast the dew of thy youth.</hi> 3. They shall be pure and clear, not muddy and corrupt, but crystal drops, as the <hi type="italic">water of life.</hi> 4. They shall be produced silently and without noise, as the dew that distils insensibly, we know not how; such is the way of the Spirit. 5. They shall live in a continual dependence upon God, and be still deriving from him, as the dew, which <hi type="italic">tarries not for man,</hi> not <hi type="italic">waits for the sons of men;</hi> they shall not rely upon human aids and powers, but on divine grace, for they are, and own that they are, no more than what the free grace of God makes them every day. 6. They shall be great blessings to those among whom they live, as the dew and the showers are to the grass, to make it grow without the help of man, or the sons of men. Their doctrine, example, and prayers, shall make them as dew, to soften and moisten others, and make them fruitful. Their speech shall <hi type="italic">distil as the dew</hi> (<reference osisRef="Deut.32.2">Deut. xxxii. 2</reference>), and all about them shall <hi type="italic">wait for them as for the rain,</hi> <reference osisRef="Job.29.23">Job xxix. 23</reference>. The people among whom they live shall be as the grass, which flourishes only by the blessing of God, and not by the art and care of man; they shall be beneficial to those about them by drawing down God's blessings on them, as Jacob on Laban's house, and by cooling and mitigating God's wrath, which otherwise would burn them up, as the dew preserves the grass from being scorched by the sun; so Dr. Pocock; they shall be mild and gentle in their behaviour, like their Master, who comes down <hi type="italic">like rain upon the new-mown grass,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ps.72.6">Ps. lxxii. 6</reference>. <div eID="gen20472" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20473" type="x-p"/> II. That they shall be <hi type="italic">as a lion among the beasts of the forest,</hi> that <hi type="italic">treads down and tears in pieces,</hi> <reference osisRef="Mic.5.8">v. 8</reference>. As they shall be silent, and gentle, and communicative of all good, to those that receive the truth in the love of it, so they shall be bold as a lion in witnessing against the corruptions of the times and places they live in, and strong as a lion, in the strength of God, to resist and overcome their spiritual enemies. The <hi type="italic">weapons of their warfare are mighty, through God, to the pulling down of strongholds,</hi> <reference osisRef="2Cor.10.4-2Cor.10.5">2 Cor. x. 4, 5</reference>. They shall have <hi type="italic">courage which all their adversaries shall not be able to resist</hi> (<reference osisRef="Luke.21.15">Luke xxi. 15</reference>), as when the lion tears none can deliver. When infidelity is silenced, and all iniquity made <hi type="italic">to stop her mouth,</hi> when sinners are convinced and converted by the power of the gospel, in the doctrine of its ministers and the conversation of its professors, then the remnant of Jacob is like a lion. This is explained, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.9">v. 9</reference>, <hi type="italic">Thy hand shall be lifted up upon thy adversaries;</hi> the church shall have the upper hand at last of all that oppose her. Her <hi type="italic">enemies shall be cut off;</hi> they shall cease to be enemies; their enmity shall be cut off. Christ's arrows of conviction shall be sharp in their hearts, so that they shall fall under him; they shall yield themselves subjects to him (<reference osisRef="Ps.45.5">Ps. xlv. 5</reference>) and be happily conquered and subdued, <reference osisRef="Ps.110.2">Ps. cx. 2</reference>. <div eID="gen20473" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20474" type="x-p"/> III. That they shall be brought off from all carnal confidences, which they have relied on, that by the providence of God they shall enjoy such a security that they shall not need them, and by the grace of God they shall be brought to see the folly of them and come off from them. It was the sin of Israel that they furnished themselves extravagantly with <hi type="italic">horses and chariots,</hi> and were <hi type="italic">soothsayers</hi> and <hi type="italic">idolaters;</hi> see <reference osisRef="Isa.2.6-Isa.2.8">Isa. ii. 6-8</reference>. But here it is promised that they shall not regard them any more. The tranquillity of the kingdom of Christ is intended in that promise, which explains this, <reference osisRef="Zech.9.10">Zech. ix. 10</reference>, <hi type="italic">I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem.</hi> Note, It is a great mercy to be deprived of those things in which we have reposed a confidence in competition with God, which we have made our arm, and after which we have gone a whoring from God. Let us observe the particulars:— 1. They had trusted in chariots and horses, and multiplied them (<reference osisRef="Ps.20.7">Ps. xx. 7</reference>); but now God will <hi type="italic">cut off their horses,</hi> and <hi type="italic">destroy their chariots</hi> (<reference osisRef="Mic.5.10">v. 10</reference>), as <hi type="italic">David houghed the chariot-horses,</hi> <reference osisRef="2Sam.8.4">2 Sam. viii. 4</reference>. They shall not have them, lest they should be tempted to trust in them. 2. They depended upon their strongholds, and fortified cities, for their security; but God will take care that they be demolished (<reference osisRef="Mic.5.11">v. 11</reference>): <hi type="italic">I will cut off the cities of thy land;</hi> I will <hi type="italic">throw down thy strongholds.</hi> They shall have them for habitations, but not for garrisons, for God will be their only place of defence, their <hi type="italic">high tower,</hi> and <hi type="italic">their deliverer.</hi> 3. Many of them depended much upon the conduct and advice of their conjurors, diviners, and fortune-tellers; and those God will cut off, not only as weak things, and insufficient to relieve them, but as wicked things, and sufficient to ruin them (<reference osisRef="Mic.5.12">v. 12</reference>): "<hi type="italic">I will cut off witchcrafts out of thy hand,</hi> that thou shalt no more take hold of them, and stay thyself upon them, and <hi type="italic">thou shalt have no more soothsayers,</hi> for thou shalt be convinced that all their pretensions are a cheat." The justice of the nation shall cut them off according to law, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.27">Lev. xx. 27</reference>. The preaching of the gospel brought men off from using curious arts, <reference osisRef="Acts.19.19">Acts xix. 19</reference>. 4. Many of them had said to the work of their hands, <hi type="italic">You are our gods;</hi> but now idolatry shall be abolished and abandoned (<reference osisRef="Mic.5.13">v. 13</reference>): "<hi type="italic">Thy graven images will I cut off, and thy standing images,</hi> both those that were movable and those that were fixed; they shall be destroyed by the power of the law of Moses and deserted by the power of the gospel of Christ, so that <hi type="italic">thou shalt no more worship the work of thy hands,</hi> but be ashamed that ever thou hast been so deluded. Among other monuments of idolatry, <hi type="italic">I will pluck up thy groves out of the midst of thee,</hi>" <reference osisRef="Mic.5.14">v. 14</reference>. These were planted and preserved in honour of their idols, and used in the worship of them; these they were ordered to burn (<reference osisRef="Deut.12.2-Deut.12.3">Deut. xii. 2, 3</reference>), and, if they do not, God will, so that they shall not have them to trust to. And so <hi type="italic">will I destroy their cities,</hi> meaning the cities that were dedicated to the idols, to some dunghill-deity or other, which they confided in for their protection. <div eID="gen20474" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20475" type="x-p"/> IV. That those who stand it out against the gospel of Christ, and continue in league with their idolatries and witchcrafts, shall fall under the wrath of God, and be consumed by it (<reference osisRef="Mic.5.15">v. 15</reference>): <hi type="italic">I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen</hi> (that is, upon heathenism), <hi type="italic">such as they have not heard;</hi> idolatries shall be done away, and idolaters put to shame. I will execute vengeance upon the heathen <hi type="italic">who have not heard</hi> (so some read it), or who would not hear and receive the doctrine of Christ. God will give his Son either the hearts or the necks of his enemies, and make them either his friends or his footstool.  <chapter eID="Mic.5"/> <div eID="gen20475" type="x-p"/>

entries.a7a0250f00dbc0ca22ab137f71c097fe578b1bba: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12768"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 5</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Mic.5.1-Mic.5.15">Mi 5:1-15</reference>. The Calamities Which Precede Messiah's Advent. His Kingdom, Conquest of Jacob's Foes, and Blessing upon His People.</title> <div sID="gen23680" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12768"/><hi type="bold">1. gather thyself in troops--</hi>that is, thou shalt do so, to resist the enemy. Lest the faithful should fall into carnal security because of the previous promises, he reminds them of the calamities which are to precede the prosperity.<div eID="gen23680" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23681" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">daughter of troops--</hi>Jerusalem is so called on account of her numerous troops.<div eID="gen23681" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23682" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">he hath laid siege--</hi>the enemy hath.<div eID="gen23682" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23683" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">they shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek--</hi>the greatest of insults to an Oriental. Zedekiah, the judge (or king, <reference osisRef="Amos.2.3">Am 2:3</reference>) of Israel, was loaded with insults by the Chaldeans; so also the other princes and judges (<reference osisRef="Lam.3.30">La 3:30</reference>). Hengstenberg thinks the expression, "the judge," marks a time when no king of the house of David reigned. The smiting on the cheek of other judges of Israel was a type of the same indignity offered to Him who nevertheless is the Judge, not only of Israel, but also of the world, and who is "from everlasting" (<reference osisRef="Mic.5.2">Mi 5:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.50.6">Is 50:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.26.67">Mt 26:67</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.27.30">27:30</reference>). <div eID="gen23683" type="x-p"/>
entries.e17b4c93f4639b2f6eb82ad698964a7803a7996b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12769"/><div sID="gen23684" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12769"/><hi type="bold">2. Beth-lehem Ephratah--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Gen.48.7">Ge 48:7</reference>), or, Beth-lehem Judah; so called to distinguish it from Beth-lehem in Zebulun. It is a few miles southwest of Jerusalem. Beth-lehem means "the house of bread"; Ephratah means "fruitful": both names referring to the fertility of the region.<div eID="gen23684" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23685" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">though thou be little among--</hi>though thou be scarcely large enough to be reckoned among, &c. It was insignificant in size and population; so that in <reference osisRef="Josh.15.21">Jos 15:21</reference>, &c., it is not enumerated among the cities of Judah; nor in the list in <reference osisRef="Neh.11.25">Ne 11:25</reference>, &c. Under Rehoboam it became a city: <reference osisRef="2Chr.11.6">2Ch 11:6</reference>, "He built Beth-lehem." <reference osisRef="Matt.2.6">Mt 2:6</reference> seems to contradict Micah, "thou art not the least," But really he, by an independent testimony of the Spirit, confirms the prophet, Little in worldly importance, thou art not least (that is, far from least, yea, the very greatest) among the thousands, of princes of Judah, in the spiritual significance of being the birthplace of Messiah (<reference osisRef="John.7.42">Joh 7:42</reference>). God chooses the little things of the world to eclipse in glory its greatest things (<reference osisRef="Judg.6.15">Jud 6:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.1.46">Joh 1:46</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.27">1Co 1:27</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.28">28</reference>). The low state of David's line when Messiah was born is also implied here.<div eID="gen23685" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23686" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thousands--</hi>Each tribe was divided into clans or "thousands" (each thousand containing a thousand families: like our old English division of counties into hundreds), which had their several heads or "princes"; hence in <reference osisRef="Matt.2.6">Mt 2:6</reference> it is quoted "princes," substantially the same as in Micah, and authoritatively explained in Matthew. It is not so much this thousand that is preferred to the other thousands of Judah, but the Governor or Chief Prince out of it, who is preferred to the governors of all the other thousands. It is called a "town" (rather in the Greek, "village"), <reference osisRef="John.7.42">Joh 7:42</reference>; though scarcely containing a thousand inhabitants, it is ranked among the "thousands" or larger divisions of the tribe, because of its being the cradle of David's line, and of the Divine Son of David. Moses divided the people into thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, with their respective "rulers" (<reference osisRef="Exod.18.25">Ex 18:25</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="1Sam.10.19">1Sa 10:19</reference>).<div eID="gen23686" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23687" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">unto me--</hi>unto God the Father (<reference osisRef="Luke.1.32">Lu 1:32</reference>): to fulfil all the Father's will and purpose from eternity. So the Son declares (<reference osisRef="Ps.2.7">Psa 2:7</reference>; 40:7, 8; <reference osisRef="John.4.34">Joh 4:34</reference>); and the Father confirms it (<reference osisRef="Matt.3.17">Mt 3:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.12.18">12:18</reference>, compare with <reference osisRef="Isa.42.1">Is 42:1</reference>). God's glory is hereby made the ultimate end of redemption.<div eID="gen23687" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23688" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ruler--</hi>the "Shiloh," "Prince of peace," "on whose shoulders the government is laid" (<reference osisRef="Gen.49.10">Ge 49:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.9.6">Is 9:6</reference>). In <reference osisRef="2Sam.23.3">2Sa 23:3</reference>, "He that ruleth over men must be just," the same Hebrew word is employed; Messiah alone realizes David's ideal of a ruler. Also in <reference osisRef="Jer.30.21">Jr 30:21</reference>, "their governor shall proceed from the midst of them"; answering closely to "out of thee shall come forth the ruler," here (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.11.1-Isa.11.4">Is 11:1-4</reference>).<div eID="gen23688" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23689" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">goings forth ... from everlasting--</hi>The plain antithesis of this clause, to "come forth out of thee" (from Beth-lehem), shows that the eternal generation of the Son is meant. The terms convey the strongest assertion of infinite duration of which the Hebrew language is capable (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.90.2">Psa 90:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.8.22">Pr 8:22</reference>, <reference osisRef="Prov.8.23">23</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.1.1">Joh 1:1</reference>). Messiah's generation as man coming forth unto God to do His will on earth is from Beth-lehem; but as Son of God, His goings forth are from everlasting. The promise of the Redeemer at first was vaguely general (<reference osisRef="Gen.3.15">Ge 3:15</reference>). Then the Shemitic division of mankind is declared as the quarter in which He was to be looked for (<reference osisRef="Gen.9.26">Ge 9:26</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.9.27">27</reference>); then it grows clearer, defining the race and nation whence the Deliverer should come, namely, the seed of Abraham, the Jews (<reference osisRef="Gen.12.3">Ge 12:3</reference>); then the particular tribe, Judah (<reference osisRef="Gen.49.10">Ge 49:10</reference>); then the family, that of David (<reference osisRef="Ps.89.19">Psa 89:19</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.89.20">20</reference>); then the very town of His birth, here. And as His coming drew nigh, the very parentage (<reference osisRef="Matt.1.1-Matt.1.17">Mt 1:1-17</reference>; Lu 1:26-35; 2:1-7); and then all the scattered rays of prophecy concentrate in Jesus, as their focus (<reference osisRef="Heb.1.1">He 1:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.1.2">2</reference>). <div eID="gen23689" type="x-p"/>
entries.f4bf03c52ac3d726fbee3d2850f44eeab5390321: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12770"/><div sID="gen23690" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12770"/>3. "Therefore (because of His settled plan) will God give up to their foes His people Israel, until," &c.<div eID="gen23690" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23691" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">she which travaileth hath brought forth--</hi>namely, "the virgin" mother, mentioned by Micah's contemporary, <reference osisRef="Isa.7.14">Is 7:14</reference>. Zion "in travail" (<reference osisRef="Mic.4.9">Mi 4:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mic.4.10">10</reference>) answers to the virgin in travail of Messiah. Israel's deliverance from her long travail-pains of sorrow will synchronize with the appearance of the Messiah as her Redeemer (<reference osisRef="Rom.11.26">Ro 11:26</reference>) in the last days, as the Church's spiritual deliverance synchronized with the virgin's giving birth to Him at His first advent. The ancient Church's travail-like waiting for Messiah is represented by the virgin's travail. Hence, both may be meant. It cannot be restricted to the Virgin Mary: for Israel is still "given up," though Messiah has been "brought forth" eighteen and a half centuries ago. But the Church's throes are included, which are only to be ended when Christ, having been preached for a witness to all nations, shall at last appear as the Deliverer of Jacob, and when the times of the Gentiles shall be fulfilled, and Israel as a nation shall be born in a day (<reference osisRef="Isa.66.7-Isa.66.11">Is 66:7-11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.21.24">Lu 21:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.12.1">Re 12:1</reference>, 2, 4; compare <reference osisRef="Rom.8.22">Ro 8:22</reference>).<div eID="gen23691" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23692" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel--</hi>(Compare <reference osisRef="Mic.4.7">Mi 4:7</reference>). The remainder of the Israelites dispersed in foreign lands shall return to join their countrymen in Canaan. The Hebrew for "unto" is, literally, "upon," implying superaddition to those already gathered. <div eID="gen23692" type="x-p"/>
entries.feb52792a82dcd7646261b4ba10deabd6226f794: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12771"/><div sID="gen23693" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12771"/><hi type="bold">4. he shall stand--</hi>that is, persevere: implying the endurance of His kingdom [Calvin]. Rather, His sedulous care and pastoral circumspection, as a shepherd stands erect to survey and guard His flock on every side (<reference osisRef="Isa.61.5">Is 61:5</reference>) [Maurer].<div eID="gen23693" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23694" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">feed--</hi>that is, rule: as the Greek word similarly in <reference osisRef="Matt.2.6">Mt 2:6</reference>, Margin, means both "feed" and "rule" (<reference osisRef="Isa.40.11">Is 40:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.49.10">49:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.34.23">Eze 34:23</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="2Sam.5.2">2Sa 5:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Sam.7.8">7:8</reference>).<div eID="gen23694" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23695" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in the majesty of the name of the Lord--</hi>possessing the majesty of all Jehovah's revealed attributes ("name") (<reference osisRef="Isa.11.2">Is 11:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Phil.2.6">Php 2:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.9">9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.2.7-Heb.2.9">He 2:7-9</reference>).<div eID="gen23695" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23696" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">his God--</hi>God is "His God" in a oneness of relation distinct from the sense in which God is our God (<reference osisRef="John.20.17">Joh 20:17</reference>).<div eID="gen23696" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23697" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">they shall abide--</hi>the Israelites ("they," namely, the returning remnant and the "children of Israel previously in Canaan) shall dwell in permanent security and prosperity (<reference osisRef="Mic.4.4">Mi 4:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.14.30">Is 14:30</reference>).<div eID="gen23697" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23698" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">unto the ends of the earth--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Mic.4.1">Mi 4:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.72.8">Psa 72:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.9.10">Zec 9:10</reference>). <div eID="gen23698" type="x-p"/>
entries.3e0208068c4ba354189d632af1a5b244063330d3: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12772"/><div sID="gen23699" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12772"/><hi type="bold">5. this man--</hi>in Hebrew simply "This." The One just mentioned; He and He alone. Emphatical for Messiah (compare <reference osisRef="Gen.5.29">Ge 5:29</reference>).<div eID="gen23699" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23700" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the peace--</hi>the fountainhead of peace between God and man, between Israel and Israel's justly offended God (<reference osisRef="Gen.49.10">Ge 49:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.9.6">Is 9:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.2.14">Ep 2:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.17">17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Col.1.20">Col 1:20</reference>), and, as the consequence, the fountain of "peace on earth," where heretofore all is strife (<reference osisRef="Mic.4.3">Mi 4:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.2.18">Ho 2:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.9.10">Zec 9:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.2.14">Lu 2:14</reference>).<div eID="gen23700" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23701" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the Assyrian--</hi>Being Israel's most powerful foe at that time, Assyria is made the representative of all the foes of Israel in all ages, who shall receive their final destruction at Messiah's appearing (<reference osisRef="Ezek.38.1-Ezek.38.23">Eze 38:1-23</reference>).<div eID="gen23701" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23702" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">seven shepherds, and eight--</hi>"Seven" expresses perfection; "seven and eight" is an idiom for a full and sufficient number (<reference osisRef="Job.5.19">Job 5:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.6.16">Pr 6:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eccl.11.2">Ec 11:2</reference>).<div eID="gen23702" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23703" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">principal men--</hi>literally, "anointed (humble) men" (<reference osisRef="Ps.62.9">Psa 62:9</reference>), such as the apostles were. Their anointing, or consecration and qualification to office, was by the Holy Spirit [Calvin] (<reference osisRef="1John.2.20">1Jo 2:20</reference>, 27). "Princes" also were anointed, and they are mentioned as under Messiah (<reference osisRef="Isa.32.1">Is 32:1</reference>). English Version therefore gives the probable sense. <div eID="gen23703" type="x-p"/>
entries.58c6bf4780928a99533498eb55370f392d399aba: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12773"/><div sID="gen23704" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12773"/><hi type="bold">6. waste--</hi>literally, "eat up": following up the metaphor of "shepherds" (compare <reference osisRef="Num.22.4">Nu 22:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.6.3">Jr 6:3</reference>).<div eID="gen23704" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23705" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">land of Nimrod--</hi>Babylon (<reference osisRef="Mic.4.10">Mi 4:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gen.10.10">Ge 10:10</reference>); or, including Assyria also, to which he extended his borders (<reference osisRef="Gen.10.11">Ge 10:11</reference>).<div eID="gen23705" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23706" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in the entrances--</hi>the passes into Assyria (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.3.21">2Ki 3:21</reference>). The Margin and Jerome, misled by a needless attention to the parallelism, "with the sword," translate, "with her own naked swords"; as in <reference osisRef="Ps.55.21">Psa 55:21</reference> the Hebrew is translated. But "in the entrances" of Assyria, answers to, "within our borders." As the Assyrians invade our borders, so shall their own borders or "entrances" be invaded.<div eID="gen23706" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23707" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">he ... he--</hi>Messiah shall deliver us, when the Assyrian shall come. <div eID="gen23707" type="x-p"/>
entries.18793122c206b5acfae9eea8484a6d7b7d80fa3e: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12774"/><div sID="gen23708" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12774"/><hi type="bold">7. remnant of Jacob--</hi>already mentioned in <reference osisRef="Mic.5.3">Mi 5:3</reference>. It in comparative smallness stands in antithesis to the "many people." Though Israel be but a remnant amidst many nations after her restoration, yet she shall exercise the same blessed influence in quickening them spiritually that the small imperceptible dew exercises in refreshing the grass (<reference osisRef="Deut.32.2">De 32:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.72.6">Psa 72:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.110.3">110:3</reference>). The influence of the Jews restored from Babylon in making many Gentile proselytes is an earnest of a larger similar effect hereafter (<reference osisRef="Isa.66.19">Is 66:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.8.13">Zec 8:13</reference>).<div eID="gen23708" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23709" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from the Lord--</hi>Israel's restoration and the consequent conversion of the Gentiles are solely of grace.<div eID="gen23709" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23710" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">tarrieth not for man--</hi>entirely God's work, as independent of human contrivance as the dew and rains that fertilize the soil. <div eID="gen23710" type="x-p"/>
entries.f9f1dc573d12ed43ecbe938552a3e71468bf996c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12775"/><div sID="gen23711" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12775"/><hi type="bold">8. as a lion--</hi>In <reference osisRef="Mic.5.7">Mi 5:7</reference> Israel's benignant influence on the nations is described; but here her vengeance on the godless hosts who assail her (<reference osisRef="Isa.66.15">Is 66:15</reference>, 16, 19, 24; <reference osisRef="Zech.12.3">Zec 12:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.6.8">6, 8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.6.9">9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.14.17">14:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.14.18">18</reference>). Judah will be "as as lion," not in respect to its cruelty, but in its power of striking terror into all opponents. Under the Maccabees, the Jews acquired Idumea, Samaria, and parts of the territory of Ammon and Moab [Grotius]. But this was only the earnest of their future glory on their coming restoration. <div eID="gen23711" type="x-p"/>
entries.8cfe331dbf18cd4672dd7f0d9cc3feeb0365f172: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12776"/><div sID="gen23712" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12776"/><hi type="bold">9. Thine hand shall be lifted up--</hi>In <reference osisRef="Isa.26.11">Is 26:11</reference> it is Jehovah's hand that is lifted up; here Israel's as <reference osisRef="Mic.5.8">Mi 5:8</reference> implies, just as "Zion" is addressed and directed to "beat in pieces many people" (<reference osisRef="Mic.4.13">Mi 4:13</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Isa.54.15">Is 54:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.54.17">17</reference>). For Israel's foes are Jehovah's foes. When her hand is said to be lifted up, it is Jehovah's hand that strikes the foe by her (compare <reference osisRef="Exod.13.9">Ex 13:9</reference>, with <reference osisRef="Exod.14.8">Ex 14:8</reference>). <div eID="gen23712" type="x-p"/>
entries.cb209d6a6314c8df9b7ebca4282a27840e2c8969: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12777"/><div sID="gen23713" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12777"/><hi type="bold">10. cut off thy horses ... chariots--</hi>namely, those used for the purposes of war. Israel had been forbidden the use of cavalry, or to go to Egypt for horses (<reference osisRef="Deut.17.16">De 17:16</reference>), lest they should trust in worldly forces, rather than in God (<reference osisRef="Ps.20.7">Psa 20:7</reference>). Solomon had disregarded this command (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.10.26">1Ki 10:26</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Kgs.10.28">28</reference>). Hereafter, saith God, I will remove these impediments to the free course of My grace: horses, chariots, &c., on which ye trust. The Church will never be safe, till she is stripped of all creature trusts, and rests on Jehovah alone [Calvin]. The universal peace given by God shall cause warlike instruments to be needless. He will cut them off from Israel (<reference osisRef="Zech.9.10">Zec 9:10</reference>); as she will cut them off from Babylon, the representative of the nations (<reference osisRef="Jer.50.37">Jr 50:37</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.51.21">51:21</reference>). <div eID="gen23713" type="x-p"/>
entries.568a353a1cf523fee01fc255191e0a6a14e60f19: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12778"/><div sID="gen23714" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12778"/><hi type="bold">11. cut off ... cities ... strongholds--</hi>such as are fortified for war. In that time of peace, men shall live in unwalled villages (<reference osisRef="Ezek.38.11">Eze 38:11</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Jer.23.6">Jr 23:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.49.31">49:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.2.8">Zec 2:8</reference>). <div eID="gen23714" type="x-p"/>
entries.47fb04cad144b59a8115f0ec075932aa8cedea4d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12779"/><div sID="gen23715" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12779"/><hi type="bold">12. witchcrafts out of thine hand--</hi>that is, which thou now usest. <div eID="gen23715" type="x-p"/>
entries.dd60b50f1645ecacc2320da441afcfaff7efac9d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12780"/><div sID="gen23716" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12780"/><hi type="bold">13. graven images ... cut off--</hi>(Compare <reference osisRef="Isa.2.8">Is 2:8</reference>, 18-21; 30:22; <reference osisRef="Zech.13.2">Zec 13:2</reference>).<div eID="gen23716" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23717" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">standing images--</hi>statues. <div eID="gen23717" type="x-p"/>
entries.3fb8b60b95ec0fa5f58ec0db81e2c2377953b14d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12781"/><div sID="gen23718" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12781"/><hi type="bold">14. groves ... cities--</hi>The "groves" are the idolatrous symbol of Astarte (<reference osisRef="Deut.16.21">De 16:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.21.7">2Ki 21:7</reference>). "Cities" being parallel to "groves," must mean cities in or near which such idolatrous groves existed. Compare "city of the house of Baal" (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.10.25">2Ki 10:25</reference>), that is, a portion of the city sacred to Baal. <div eID="gen23718" type="x-p"/>
entries.30bfccb150dc2bc6a92ed7fb4371bdc5dd98cf77: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12782"/><div sID="gen23719" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12782"/><hi type="bold">15. vengeance ... such as they have not heard--</hi>or, as the Hebrew order favors, "the nations that have not hearkened to My warnings." So the Septuagint (<reference osisRef="Ps.149.7">Psa 149:7</reference>). <chapter eID="Mic.5"/>

entries.7df05d284010c1b06b6f81f66f5b139cb00f5499: <div eID="gen34808" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen34809" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen34810" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen34810" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen34809" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen34811" type="x-p"/> This chapter begins, according to the opinion of some commentators, with a prophecy concerning the siege of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar, and the great indignities which Zedekiah should suffer from the Babylonians, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.1">Mic 5:1</reference>. We have next a most famous prediction concerning the birthplace of the Messiah, "whose goings forth have been from of old, from Everlasting, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.2">Mic 5:2</reference>. See <reference osisRef="Mat.2.6">Mat 2:6</reference>. The Jews obstinately persisting in their opposition to the Messiah, God will therefore give them up into the hands of their enemies till the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled: and then all the posterity of Jacob, both Israel and Judah, shall be converted to the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, and, along with the Gentiles, be brought into the large and peaceful pastures of this Great Shepherd of the sheep, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.3">Mic 5:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.4">Mic 5:4</reference>. After this illustrious prophecy, the prophet goes on to foretell the downfall of the Assyrians, by whom are meant the enemies of the Church in general, the type being probably put for the antitype; the miraculous discomfiture of the great Assyrian army in the reign of Sennacherib strongly shadowing forth the glorious and no less miraculous triumphs of Christianity in the latter times, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.5">Mic 5:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.6">Mic 5:6</reference>. See <reference osisRef="Isa.11.16">Isa 11:16</reference>. Some understand this prophecy of Antiochus and the seven famous Maccabees, with their eight royal successors, from Aristobulus to Antigonus; and it is not impossible that these people may be also intended, for we have often had occasion to remark that a prophecy of the Old Testament Scriptures has frequently more than one aspect. The seventh verse was fulfilled by the Jews spreading the knowledge of the true God during their captivity, and so paving the way for the gospel; but will be more signally fulfilled after their conversion and restoration. See <reference osisRef="Rom.11.12-Rom.11.15">Rom 11:12-15</reference>. The remaining verses contain a prophecy of the final overthrow of all the enemies of pure and undefiled religion, and of the thorough purification of the Church of God from the corruptions of Antichrist, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.9-Mic.5.15">Mic 5:9-15</reference>. <div eID="gen34811" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34812" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen34812" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34813" type="x-p"/> O daughter of troops - The Chaldeans, whose armies were composed of troops from various nations. <div eID="gen34813" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34814" type="x-p"/> He (Nebuchadnezzar) hath laid siege against us; (Jerusalem ); they shall smite the judge of Israel (Zedekiah) with a rod upon the cheek - They shall offer him the greatest indignity. They slew his sons before his face; and then put out his eyes, loaded him with chains, and carried him captive to Babylon.
entries.078dc7db96ac76e2ba84bd979eb255a48ccb08bf: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen34814" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34815" type="x-p"/> But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah - I have considered this subject in great detail in the notes on <reference osisRef="Mat.2.6">Mat 2:6</reference>, to which the reader will be pleased to refer. This verse should begin this chapter; the first verse belongs to the preceding chapter. <div eID="gen34815" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34816" type="x-p"/> Bethlehem Ephratah, to distinguish it from another Beth-lehem, which was in the tribe of Zebulun, <reference osisRef="Jos.19.15">Jos 19:15</reference>. <div eID="gen34816" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34817" type="x-p"/> Thousands of Judah - The tribes were divided into small portions called thousands; as in our country certain divisions of counties are called hundreds. <div eID="gen34817" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34818" type="x-p"/> Whose goings forth have been from of old - In every age, from the foundation of the world, there has been some manifestation of the Messiah. He was the hope, as he was the salvation, of the world, from the promise to Adam in paradise, to his manifestation in the flesh four thousand years after. <div eID="gen34818" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34819" type="x-p"/> From everlasting - מימי עולם miyemey olam, "From the days of all time;" from time as it came out of eternity. That is, there was no time in which he has not been going forth-coming in various ways to save men. And he that came forth the moment that time had its birth, was before that time in which he began to come forth to save the souls that he had created. He was before all things. As he is the Creator of all things, so he is the Eternal, and no part of what was created. All being but God has been created. Whatever has not been created is God. But Jesus is the Creator of all things; therefore he is God; for he cannot be a part of his own work.
entries.c5c3a624caae448fce368e10b3010d57b059c35f: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen34819" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34820" type="x-p"/> Therefore wilt he give them up - Jesus Christ shall give up the disobedient and rebellious Jews into the hands of all the nations of the earth, till she who travaileth hath brought forth; that is, till the Christian Church, represented <reference osisRef="Rev.12.1">Rev 12:1</reference>, under the notion of a woman in travail, shall have had the fullness of the Gentiles brought in. Then the remnant of his brethren shall return; the Jews also shall be converted unto the Lord; and thus all Israel shall be saved according to <reference osisRef="Rom.11.26">Rom 11:26</reference>. <div eID="gen34820" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34821" type="x-p"/> Unto the children of Israel - Taking in both families, that of Judah and that of Israel. The remnant of the ten tribes, wherever they are, shall be brought in under Christ; and though now lost among the nations of the earth, they will then not only be brought in among the fullness of the Gentiles, but most probably be distinguished as Jews. <div eID="gen34821" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34822" type="x-p"/> On this verse Abp. Newcome says, "The sense is, God will not fully vindicate and exalt his people, till the virgin mother shall have brought forth her Son; and till Judah and Israel, and all the true sons of Abraham among their brethren the Gentiles, be converted to Christianity.
entries.21c75bb0f64d869184ed7f8b9e85ded66aceeab2: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen34822" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34823" type="x-p"/> He shall stand and feed - The Messiah shall remain with his followers, supporting and governing them in the strength and majesty of the Lord, with all the miraculous interferences of his power, and all the glories of his grace. <div eID="gen34823" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34824" type="x-p"/> And they shall abide - After this the Jews shall no more go astray, but shall remain one people with the Gentiles, under the one Shepherd and Bishop of all souls. <div eID="gen34824" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34825" type="x-p"/> Newcome translates, "They shall be converted" for instead of וישבו veyashebu, he reads וישובו veyashubu, which gives him the translation above. This is the reading of three MSS. of Kennicott's and De Rossi's, with the Syriac, Chaldee, and Vulgate. <div eID="gen34825" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34826" type="x-p"/> For now shall he be great - The Messiah shall be great, as bringing salvation to the ends of the earth. All nations shall receive his religion, and he shall be universal King.
entries.d4b77d6c88839c90b74ed21d35fd28074d34efde: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen34826" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34827" type="x-p"/> And this man shall be the peace - This clause should be joined to the preceding verse, as it finishes the prophecy concerning our blessed Lord, who is the Author and Prince of Israel; and shall finally give peace to all nations, by bringing them under his yoke. <div eID="gen34827" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34828" type="x-p"/> When the Assyrian shall come - This is a new prophecy, and relates to the subversion of the Assyrian empire. <div eID="gen34828" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34829" type="x-p"/> Then shall we raise against him seven shepherds - Supposed to mean the seven Maccabees, Mattathias, and his five sons, and Hyrcanus, the son of Simon. <div eID="gen34829" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34830" type="x-p"/> Eight principal men - Eight princes, the Asmonean race; beginning with Aristobulus, and ending with Herod, who was married to Mariamne. - Sharpe. Perhaps seven and eight are a definite for an indefinite number, as <reference osisRef="Ecc.11.2">Ecc 11:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.5.19">Job 5:19</reference>. The prophet means the chiefs of the Medes and Babylonians, the prefects of different provinces who took Nineveh, whose number may have been what is here specified. - Newcome. <div eID="gen34830" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34831" type="x-p"/> Calmet considers this as referring to the invasion of Judea by Cambyses, when the Lord raised up against him the seven magi. He of them who passed for king of the Persians was the Smerdis of Herodotus, the Oropastes of Trogus, and the Artaxerxes of Ezra. These magi were put to death by seven Persian chiefs; who, having delivered the empire from them, set one of themselves, Darius, the son of Hystaspes, upon the throne.
entries.6e0297567df061843cf29929f753adce798cd553: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen34831" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34832" type="x-p"/> The land of Nimrod - Assyria, and Nineveh its capital; and Babylon, which was also built by Nimrod, who was its first king, <reference osisRef="Gen.10.11">Gen 10:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.10.12">Gen 10:12</reference>, in the margin. <div eID="gen34832" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34833" type="x-p"/> In the entrances thereof - At its posts or watergates; for it was by rendering themselves masters of the Euphrates that the Medes and Persians took the city, according to the prediction of Jeremiah, <reference osisRef="Jer.51.32">Jer 51:32</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.51.36">Jer 51:36</reference>. Calmet thinks that this refers to the deliverance of the land from Cambyses by his death, and the insurrection of the eight princes mentioned above, who made themselves masters of the whole Babylonian empire, etc. Perhaps it is best to refer it to the invasion of Judea by Nebuchadnezzar; and the final destruction of the Babylonish empire by Cyrus, who took Babylon, slew Belshazzar, and possessed himself of the kingdom.
entries.e75f1c4c13f7a76c96500880998f8de459b189b4: <hi type="bold">Verse 7</hi> <div eID="gen34833" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34834" type="x-p"/> The remnant of Jacob - From the reign of Darius Hystaspes (Ahasuerus, husband of Esther) the Jews were greatly favored. Those who continued in Persia and Chaldea were greatly honored under the protection of Mordecai and Esther. - Calmet. But others consider this as applying to the Maccabees. <div eID="gen34834" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34835" type="x-p"/> As a dew from the Lord - Even during their captivity many of the Jews were the means of spreading the knowledge of the one true God; see <reference osisRef="Dan.2.47">Dan 2:47</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.3.29">Dan 3:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.4.34">Dan 4:34</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.6.26">Dan 6:26</reference>. This may be the dew from the Lord mentioned here. When the Messiah appeared, the Gospel was preached by them; and it shall again be propagated by their future glorious restoration, <reference osisRef="Rom.11.12">Rom 11:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rom.11.25">Rom 11:25</reference>. <div eID="gen34835" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34836" type="x-p"/> The grass, that tarrieth not for man - Which grass springs up without the attention and culture of man; לאיש leish, even the best and most skillful of men. <div eID="gen34836" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34837" type="x-p"/> Nor waiteth for the sons of men - לבני אדם libney adam, for the sons of Adam, the first transgressor. The dew and the showers descend on the earth and water it, in order to render it fruitful; and the grass springs up independently either of the worth or wickedness of man. All comes through God's bounty, who causes his sun to shine on the just and the unjust, and his rain to descend on the evil and the good.
entries.55088e32090d65eda87a12a75ec2a59a137bb836: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen34837" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34838" type="x-p"/> As a lion - In this and the following verse the victories of the Maccabees are supposed to be foretold.
entries.2bf11f640cc6ac444634bb22a2eb3979e71aff43: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen34838" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34839" type="x-p"/> All thine enemies shall be cut off - The Assyrians, who had destroyed Israel; and the Babylonians, who had ruined Judah.
entries.1c1a159eb10a4115090c946618612f6ad36a8d60: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen34839" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34840" type="x-p"/> I will cut off thy horses - Thou shalt have no need of cavalry in thine armies; God will fight for you.
entries.8518895616cee9780cb9097d20a839559ccd6f0b: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen34840" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34841" type="x-p"/> I will - throw down all thy strongholds - Thou shalt have no need of fortified cities; I will be thy defense.
entries.466701e2bb83b661c4a6f8a0af446f5ba80151c1: <hi type="bold">Verse 12</hi> <div eID="gen34841" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34842" type="x-p"/> I will cut off witchcrafts - Thou shalt seek help only in Jehovah thy God. They have had neither soothsayers, images, groves, nor high places, from the captivity to the present day.
entries.199d51390f585e0a3dd55db14b042d144d18bd55: <hi type="bold">Verse 13</hi> <div eID="gen34842" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34843" type="x-p"/> Thy graven images also will I cut off - Thou shalt be no more an idolatrous people.
entries.ec0cc0b2ca9b71119327af12ca540d0da99e3bf8: <hi type="bold">Verse 15</hi> <div eID="gen34843" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34844" type="x-p"/> I will execute vengeance - upon the heathen - And he did so; for the empires of the Assyrians, Chaldeans, and others, the sworn enemies of the Jews, have long since been utterly destroyed.  <chapter eID="Mic.5"/> <div eID="gen34844" type="x-p"/>

entries.87fb787d1f3fe1bf5928238363f646d5078797f5: Mic 5:1 (Hebrew_Bible_4:14). “Now wilt thou gather in troops, thou daughter of troops; they lay siege against us; with the staff they smite the judge of Israel upon the cheek.” With <hi type="italic">‛attâh</hi> (now) the prophet’s address turns once more to the object introduced with <hi type="italic">‛attâh</hi> in Mic 4:9. For we may see clearly enough from the omission of the cop. <hi type="italic">Vav</hi>, which could not be left out if it were intended to link on Mic 5:1 to Mic 4:11-13, that this <hi type="italic">‛attâh</hi> points back to Mic 4:9, and is not attached to the <hi type="italic">ve‛attâh</hi> in Mic 4:11, for the purpose of introducing a fresh occurrence to follow the event mentioned in Mic 4:11-13. “The prophecy in Mic 4:11-13 explains the ground of that in Mic 4:9, Mic 4:10, and the one in Mic 5:1 sounds like a conclusion drawn from this explanation. The explanation in Mic 4:11-13 is enclosed on both sides by that which it explains. By returning in Mic 5:1 to the thoughts expressed in Mic 4:9, the prophet rounds off the strophe in 4:9-5:1” (Caspari). The words are addressed to the daughter Zion, who alone is addressed with every <hi type="italic">‛attâh</hi>, and generally throughout the entire section. <hi type="italic">Bath</hi>-<hi type="italic">gegūd</hi>, daughter of the troop, might mean: thou nation accustomed or trained to form troops, thou warlike Zion. But this does not apply to what follows, in which a siege alone is mentioned. This turn is given to the expression, rather “for the purpose of suggesting the thought of a crowd of people pressing anxiously together, as distinguished from <hi type="italic">gedūd</hi>, an invading troop.” The verb <hi type="italic">hithgōdēd</hi> does not mean here to scratch one’s self or make incisions (<reference osisRef="Deut.14.1">Deu 14:1</reference>, etc.), but, as in <reference osisRef="Jer.5.7">Jer 5:7</reference>, to press or crowd together; and the thought is this: Now crowd together with fear in a troop, for he (sc., the enemy) sets, or prepares, a siege against us. In עלינוּ the prophet includes himself in the nation as being a member of it. He finds himself in spirit along with the people besieged Zion. The siege leads to conquest; for it is only in consequence of this that the judge of Israel can be smitten with the rod upon the cheek, i.e., be shamefully ill treated (compare 1Ki 22:24; <reference osisRef="Ps.3.8">Psa 3:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.16.10">Job 16:10</reference>). The judge of Israel, whether the king or the Israelitish judges comprehended in one, cannot be thought of as outside the city at the time when the city is besieged. Of all the different effects of the siege of the city the prophet singles out only this one, viz., the ill-treatment of the judge, because “nothing shows more clearly how much misery and shame Israel will have to endure for its present sins” (Caspari). “The judge of Israel” is the person holding the highest office in Israel. This might be the king, as in <reference osisRef="Amos.2.3">Amo 2:3</reference> (cf. <reference osisRef="1Sam.8.5-1Sam.8.6">1Sa 8:5-6</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Sam.8.20">1Sa 8:20</reference>), since the Israelitish king was the supreme judge in Israel, or the true possessor of the judicial authority and dignity. But the expression is hardly to be restricted to the king, still less is it meant in distinction from the king, as pointing back to the time when Israel had no king, and was only governed by judges; but the judge stands for the king here, on the one hand with reference to the threat in Mic 3:1, Mic 3:9, Mic 3:11, where the heads and princes of Israel are described as unjust and ungodly judges, and on the other hand as an antithesis to <hi type="italic">mōshēl</hi> in Mic 5:2. As the Messiah is not called king there, but <hi type="italic">mōshēl</hi>, ruler, as the possessor of supreme authority; so here the possessor of judicial authority is called <hi type="italic">shōphēt</hi>, to indicate the reproach which would fall upon the king and the leaders of the nation on account of their unrighteousness. The threat in this verse does not refer, however, to the Roman invasion. Such an idea can only be connected with the assumption already refuted, that Mic 4:11-13 point to the times of the Maccabees, and no valid argument can be adduced to support it. In the verse before us the prophet reverts to the oppression predicted in Mic 4:9 and Mic 4:10, so that the remarks already made in Mic 4:10 apply to the fulfilment of what is predicted here. The principal fulfilment occurred in the Chaldaean period; but the fulfilment was repeated in every succeeding siege of Jerusalem until the destruction of the city by the Romans. For, according to Mic 5:3, Israel will be given up to the power of the empire of the world until the coming of the Messiah; that is to say, not merely till His birth or public appearance, but till the nation shall accept the Messiah, who has appeared as its own Redeemer.
entries.13057e0bfe6b3e29b19937378a748cdc05d4f912: Mic 5:2 (Hebrew_Bible_5:1) <div eID="gen16571" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16572" type="x-p"/> The previous announcement of the glory to which Zion is eventually to attain, is now completed by the announcement of the birth of the great Ruler, who through His government will lead Israel to this, the goal of its divine calling. Mic 5:2. <hi type="italic">“And thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, too small to be among the thousands of Judah, out of thee will He come forth to me who will be Ruler over Israel; and His goings forth are from the olden time, from the days of eternity.” </hi> The ואתּה, with which this new section of the proclamation of salvation opens, corresponds to the ואתּה in Mic 4:8. Its former government is to return to Zion (Mic 4:8), and out of little Bethlehem is the possessor of this government to proceed, viz., the Ruler of Israel, who has sprung from eternity. This thought is so attached to Mic 5:1, that the divine exaltation of the future Ruler of Israel is contrasted with the deepest degradation of the judge. The names <hi type="italic">Bethlehem Ephratah</hi> (<hi type="italic">'Ephrâth</hi> and <hi type="italic">'Ephrâthâh</hi>, i.e., the fertile ones, or the fruit-fields, being the earlier name; by the side of which <hi type="italic">Bēth</hi>-<hi type="italic">lechem</hi>, bread-house, had arisen even in the patriarchal times: see <reference osisRef="Gen.35.19">Gen 35:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gen.48.7">Gen 48:7</reference>; Rth 4:11) are connected together to give greater solemnity to the address, and not to distinguish the Judaean Bethlehem from the one in Zebulun (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.15">Jos 19:15</reference>), since the following words, “among the thousands of Judah,” provide sufficiently for this. In the little town the inhabitants are addressed; and this explains the masculines אתּה, צעיר, and ממּך, as the prophet had them in his mind when describing the smallness of the little town, which is called κώμη in Joh 7:42. צעיר להיות, literally “small with regard to the being among the <hi type="italic">'ălâphı̄m</hi> of Judah,” i.e., too small to have a place among them.
